newsitem.title: DUBAI: Start of Ramadan slows trade in UAE stocks.
newsitem.headline: Start of Ramadan slows trade in UAE stocks.

text.p: Trade on the unofficial United Arab Emirates stock market was slow in the week to Thursday with the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, dealers said.
The National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) 27-share index rose 12.41 points to 2,504.75 from 2,492.34.
Dealers said trade was limited to a few shares of banks and some companies in the first week of Ramadan, when Moslems fast during daylight hours.

Shares of market leader Etisalat, the telecommunications company, rose to 960 dirhams after weeks of holding steady at 955 dirhams. Dealers said the shares rose on expectations that the company would soon distribute dividends to shareholders.
Commercial Bank of Dubai shares rose four dirhams to 64 dirhams while Dubai Islamic Bank shares declined to 185 dirhams from 187 dirhams. Most other shares were flat.
